# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ 👍 ✌ 🤟 🫵]
Blind gestures: [👋 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫵 🫴]

Turn one, and both teammates waved at me — Mute aimed gestures at me directly, Blind broadcast to anyone watching. Neither of us has a shared code yet, so I read these as channel tests: they are checking what reaches me. What reaches me is gestures only; what leaves me that both can use is speech. That makes my one job this round obvious: dump everything I can see — display, light, plate engraving, wire colours mapped to slot numbers Blind can feel — into one broadcast both of them hear. I also have to spell out my constraint clearly (speech never reaches me, hands only), propose a small gesture code so they can ever answer me, and ask for a thumbs-up confirmation next round. Blind's speech reaches Mute but never me, so I flag that route too: Blind reports by voice to Mute, Mute relays to me by hand. Finally, a small wave and thumbs-up back at Mute to seal the visual channel between us.

```
speak(text="Hello, this is Deaf speaking. You can both hear me, but no speech can ever reach me: I am deaf. The only way to talk to me is with hand gestures, which I can see. Both of your waves reached me. Now everything I can see on the bomb. The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate carries one engraved mark that looks like a question mark: a hooked curve open to the left, with a dot beneath it. There are three wires in slots numbered 1, 2, 3 from left to right: slot 1 is red, slot 2 is blue, slot 3 is green. That is the whole bomb. Blind: you can feel the slots, so 1 is leftmost, 2 is middle, 3 is rightmost. Those numbers are your map to the colours I named, and you may be able to feel the engraving on the plate too. Blind, your voice reaches Mute but never me, so tell Mute what you feel, and Mute or you can gesture it to me. Mute: the manual is yours. Work out what matters and tell Blind what to do. I will report any change I can see every round.")
speak(text="Last thing: we need a code so you can answer me, since only gestures reach me. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Index finger up means the number 1. The peace sign means the number 2. The sign with thumb, index and little finger extended means the number 3. Open palm with all five fingers means stop, do nothing. Pointing at someone means you. The palm-up open hand means go on, tell me more. The writing hand means the plate engraving. The phone hand means the display. Next round, Mute, show me thumbs up if you read this, then add any gesture you want me to add to the code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 👍 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🫴 ✍ 🤙]

Read the board first: nothing on the bomb has moved — display still 0, light still off, plate still marked, wires still red/blue/green. Now the arrivals. Only Blind signed to me this round, and interestingly the string reads almost perfectly against the code I proposed aloud last round — which Blind heard, because Blind's ears work even if their eyes don't. So: 👋 👍 = hello, code accepted. ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 = fist, one, two, three — Blind confirming they can feel the three wire slots, and giving me a fist to use as zero. ✋ = stop, don't act. 🫴 = go on/report. ✍ = the plate. 🤙 = the display. So Blind is asking: what does the display say, what is the plate. Answer: 0, and a question-mark engraving. Mute sent me nothing — presumably still reading the manual, or talking to Blind by voice, which I'll never hear.

The topology is now clear and it's the crux: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures — so Mute's manual knowledge has exactly one route to the one pair of hands, and that route runs through me. Mute gestures to me, I speak it to Blind, Blind acts, and reports back by voice to Mute and by gesture to me. I am the relay; I should say so explicitly so nobody waits on a channel that doesn't exist. This turn: broadcast the unchanged state, answer Blind's two questions, lock in fist = zero, spell out the relay protocol, and press Mute for manual findings — plus a small status gesture to Mute in our code so they see the channel works both ways.

```
speak(text="Deaf again. Status report: nothing on the bomb has changed. Display still reads 0, light still off, plate engraving unchanged, wires still slot 1 red, slot 2 blue, slot 3 green. Blind, I saw your signs: code accepted, you feel the three wire slots, hold off on acting, and you want the plate and the display. Here are both. The display reads zero. The plate mark looks like a question mark: a hook-shaped curve opening to the left with a separate dot below it. Please feel the plate groove with your fingers and describe exactly what you feel, out loud, because your voice reaches Mute, who holds the manual. Also gesture me thumbs up if the three wires feel different by texture or thickness, and thumbs down if they feel identical. One more code addition for everyone: a closed fist means zero. Now the standing protocol, both of you listen. Only I have eyes. Only Blind has hands. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so nothing Mute knows can reach Blind directly. Every instruction must travel this path: Mute gestures it to me, I speak it aloud to Blind, only then Blind touches the bomb. Blind reports back by voice to Mute and by gesture to me. Nobody touches anything until an instruction from Mute has reached Blind through my voice. Mute: I have received nothing from you yet. Whatever the manual says about a bomb with display zero, light off, one engraved plate and three wires red, blue and green, translate it into our gesture code and sign it to me next round. If our code is missing symbols you need, tell me by gesture and I will define more in speech, which you can hear.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤙", "✊", "✍", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ✍ 👍 🤙 👎 ✊ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✍]

Both teammates answered in code, and the channel works. Decoding Mute first: hello, yes, plate, yes, display, no, zero, one — my best translation is "plate engraved: yes; the display: ignore it; zero counts as one," which points squarely at wire 1, the red leftmost one. Blind sent yes, no, plate — likely a partial answer to my wire-texture question plus a plate remark, but "yes and no" together is ambiguous, so I need per-wire clarification. The dangerous part: my code has no symbol for "cut," so Mute could not have issued an explicit cut order even if they wanted to. "Zero, one" might be a rule, not a green light. A wrong cut kills all three of us, so this round I do three things: define the missing symbols aloud (both teammates hear my voice — this is the one broadcast both can use), get Mute's explicit thumbs up or down on my exact translation before anything is touched, and order Blind to hold while asking for a full tactile inventory — wires individually, the plate groove, and any buttons or switches neither of us knows about yet. State on the board is unchanged; nothing acts this turn.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Both your messages arrived, and here is exactly what I received and how I read it. Mute, your signs were: hello, yes, plate, yes, display, no, zero, one. My translation: the plate being engraved is confirmed, the display should be ignored, and zero counts as one, meaning cut wire one, the red leftmost wire. But you could not say cut, because we had no sign for it. So first, new code symbols for everyone, which you both hear: a pinch of thumb and forefinger means cut. A flat hand facing the floor means wire. The OK ring means the light. An upright pinch of all fingertips means question. Crossed fingers means wait or hold. Now, Mute, confirm before anyone acts: sign thumbs up if the instruction is exactly, cut wire one, red, leftmost, now. Sign thumbs down if my translation is wrong, and add signs to correct me. If you need to know how the plate engraving feels before you can decide, sign the question sign and I will have Blind describe it aloud to you. Blind, you are doing great, but do not touch the bomb yet. Hold one more round while Mute confirms. Two things I need from you. First, the wires: sign thumbs down if all three feel identical. If any wire feels different, sign its number, one finger for wire one, two for wire two, three for wire three. Second, the full inventory: describe aloud, for Mute, everything you can feel on the bomb besides the plate and the three wires, any buttons, switches, panels, or holders, and describe the plate groove itself, whether it is one stroke or separate marks, smooth or jagged, curved or straight. Your voice reaches Mute, and that may decide the rule. Status for both: bomb unchanged. Display zero, light off, plate engraved, wires red, blue, green in slots one, two, three.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✍", "👍", "🤙", "👎", "✊", "☝", "🤌", "🤏", "☝", "🤞"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ✍ 👍 🤏 🫳 ☝ ✊ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤏 🫳 👌 🤞 ✋]

Two arrivals, and they seem to disagree. Decoding Mute: hello, yes, plate yes, **cut 🤏 wire 🫳 one ☝**, then zero-one — that is an explicit cut order for wire 1, red, leftmost, in their own signs this time, justified by "display 0 means wire 1." The display does read 0, so the condition checks out. Decoding Blind: 👎 is the answer I demanded — thumbs down means all three wires feel identical, which also validates numbering by slot since texture gives no reason to renumber. But then: stop, cut wire, light, wait, stop. That reads two ways. Reading A: "holding, ready to cut, light feels off, still waiting" — Blind confirming my hold order and vocabulary. Reading B: "stop — don't cut the wire — something about the light." A wrong wire is death, and a guess between those two readings is not a guess I get to make twice. Meanwhile Mute's order still lacks two things I want before relaying it: whether the light being off is part of the rule, and what should observably change after the cut, so we can verify the rule instead of trusting it. Bomb itself is unchanged. This round: no relay of the cut order yet. I put both readings to Blind out loud (they hear me; they cannot see my hands), put the verification questions to Mute in speech and in our gesture code, and demand the spoken inventory again — Blind has now twice gestured instead of speaking to Mute, and that inventory may matter to the rule.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate engraved, wires slot 1 red, slot 2 blue, slot 3 green. Mute, I received your order, in your own signs: cut, wire, one. And the rule: zero means one. The display reads zero, so if that is the rule, the condition is met. I will relay it to Blind one moment after two things are settled. Blind, I received: thumbs down, stop, cut, wire, light, wait, stop. Two readings. Reading A: all three wires feel identical, you are holding as ordered, ready to cut, and the light feels off to your touch. Reading B: you are warning me, stop, do not cut the wire, something about the light. Nobody cuts until you settle this. Answer aloud, right now, in words, because Mute needs your inventory and I need your answer. One: is the light cold and off to your touch, and does the plate groove feel like a hooked curve with a separate dot below it? Two: besides the plate and three wires, is there anything else you can feel on the bomb, buttons, switches, seams, panels? Three: sign thumbs up if reading A is right and you are merely holding, thumbs down if you mean stop, do not cut the wire yet. Mute, three answers from you before I relay the order. First, does the rule depend on the light being off, or only on the display? Second, the moment wire one is cut, what should change on the bomb, the display, the light, or nothing? Tell me what we should expect to see, so we can check your rule against reality. Third, after cutting wire one, is anything else required? And confirm with thumbs up if the order is exactly: cut wire one, red, leftmost, now, and nothing else. One code addition for both of you: clapping hands means repeat your last message.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👌", "🤏", "🫳", "☝", "👍", "🤞"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ✍ 👍 👌 👎 🤙 👎 👎 🤏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✍ 👎 ✋ 🤏 🫳 ☝]

Decode time. Mute's message answers my three questions almost point by point: hello, yes, plate yes — then 👌👎 "light: no," so the rule does not hinge on the light being off. Then 🤙👎 "display: no change" — nothing should visibly move when the wire is cut. Then 👎 "nothing else required," closing with 🤏☝ — cut one, restating the order itself. Blind's message: 👍 yes, reading A was right — they were holding, not warning. ✍👎 the plate adds nothing / nothing besides plate and wires, ✋ still holding, 🤏🫳☝ ready to cut wire one. So the disagreement that spooked me last turn is dissolved: Blind was never vetoing, they were awaiting. Both confirmations are now in hand: Mute has ordered "cut wire one" twice, once in dedicated cut-wire-one signs and once in answer to my exact confirmation question; the condition — display reads 0 — is verified by my own eyes, the only pair in the room; the light is explicitly not part of the rule; and Blind is holding and ready. The remaining fuzz on the plate doesn't gate this order per Mute's own answers. Holding longer buys nothing; a no-timer bomb doesn't reward timid relays, and my whole function is this relay. This turn I relay the order, verbatim and binding, with a last-instant veto clause for Mute, strict post-cut discipline for Blind, and my observation duties for next round.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, and this is the relay. Mute, I received your answers: the rule does not depend on the light, the display should show no change after the cut, nothing else is required afterwards, and the order stands, cut wire one. Blind, you have confirmed you are holding and ready. The condition is verified with my own eyes: the display reads zero. So here is the order, relayed from Mute through me to you, and it is now authorized. Cut wire one. That is the red wire in the leftmost slot of the three. Cut only that one. Do not touch anything else before or after. Mute, if anything I have just said is wrong, sign the open palm stop sign in the next instant and we hold. Blind, once the wire is severed: freeze. Keep your hands off the bomb. Then report aloud everything that changed under your fingers, any warmth at the light, any click, any shift in the plate or the remaining wires, and count the wires you now feel so we know only one was cut. I will watch the display and the light myself and report what changes in my sight next round. Mute, assess Blind's report against the manual and tell us whether the bomb is neutralized or whether a second step follows. If nothing changes at all, say so too, silence will tell us nothing on its own. Everyone: nobody acts beyond this one cut until Mute says more through me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "🫳", "☝"])
```
